novel_features.name: Net worth + trajectory
novel_features.description: Total net worth across every institution, with a balance trajectory over time no bank app can show.
novel_features.rationale: Requires summing balances across all connections in the local store and joining a balance-snapshot time series the protocol never returns.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when an agent needs a single cross-institution net-worth number or its trend; no single /accounts call gives history.

novel_features.name: Cash flow analysis
novel_features.description: Income vs outflow by month and top-spend merchants across all accounts.
novel_features.rationale: GROUP BY month and signed-amount aggregation over the local transaction store, spanning institutions a single bank view can't.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for spending/income rollups; the API returns raw transactions, not aggregates.

novel_features.name: Recurring/subscription detection
novel_features.description: Surfaces subscriptions and regular obligations by detecting repeated payees with regular cadence.
novel_features.rationale: Interval-pattern detection over the local store across all institutions at once; not an API capability.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to find recurring charges hiding across multiple accounts before they surprise the user.

novel_features.name: Holdings gain/loss
novel_features.description: Investment positions with market value vs cost basis and total gain/loss across brokerages.
novel_features.rationale: Computes market_value minus cost_basis per holding from the local holding table; almost no SimpleFIN tool implements holdings at all.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for portfolio gain/loss; the ecosystem-wide gap means this data is otherwise invisible.

novel_features.name: Rules-based categorization
novel_features.description: Assigns categories to transactions with deterministic keyword/regex rules (the protocol has none).
novel_features.rationale: SimpleFIN ships zero categories; local rules fill the gap without depending on an LLM or external service.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run before cashflow to get category breakdowns; deterministic and offline.

novel_features.name: Ledger/plaintext export
novel_features.description: Exports the local ledger to ledger, beancount, csv, or qif for plaintextaccounting tools.
novel_features.rationale: Serializes the local transaction store into accounting formats SimpleFIN can't emit.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to bridge into Beancount/Ledger/GnuCash workflows.

novel_features.name: Content-based dedup
novel_features.description: Finds and merges duplicate transactions created by SimpleFIN's unstable, mirrored IDs using content hashing.
novel_features.rationale: Hashes amount+date+normalized description over the local store; fixes the protocol's own #1 defect that breaks every importer.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run after sync to detect duplicate charges that ID-based dedup misses.

novel_features.name: Recent activity since last check
novel_features.description: What's new across all accounts since a date or your last sync — new transactions and balance changes, neutrally framed.
novel_features.rationale: Diffs the local store against a point in time across every institution; the API only returns point-in-time state, not 'what changed'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for a quick 'what happened lately' digest across accounts without scanning every transaction.

narrative.headline: Pull every bank, card, and brokerage account through SimpleFIN into a local SQLite ledger — with net worth, cash flow, recurring-charge detection, and holdings gain/loss no single bank app can show.
narrative.value_prop: Every existing SimpleFIN tool is an importer into someone else's app. This is a CLI and a local database you own: sync once (rate-limit aware), then run cross-institution analytics offline. networth tracks your trajectory over time, recurring surfaces hidden subscriptions, portfolio computes holdings gain/loss the ecosystem ignores, and export bridges into Beancount/Ledger.
narrative.auth_narrative: SimpleFIN has no API key. You claim a base64 Setup Token to receive an Access URL (https://user:pass@host/simplefin) that bakes in HTTP Basic credentials and the server host. Run 'simplefin-pp-cli auth claim <setup-token>' once (or set SIMPLEFIN_ACCESS_URL); the access URL is stored chmod 600 and never logged. A reusable public demo token is available at beta-bridge.simplefin.org/info/developers for testing.

quickstart.comment: Health check — confirms the binary and config before you connect.
Pull all institutions into the local store (one call, rate-limit aware).
See total net worth across every account and its trajectory.
Monthly income-vs-outflow as structured JSON for agents.

troubleshoots.fix: The access URL was revoked or is wrong. Re-claim: simplefin-pp-cli auth claim <new-setup-token>.
SimpleFIN allows ~24 requests/day. Avoid scripted loops; one sync pulls all accounts. Run simplefin-pp-cli doctor to see quota guidance.
Pass a window: simplefin-pp-cli sync --since 90d. A single call is capped at 90 days; the local store accumulates history across syncs.
SimpleFIN reuses/mirrors transaction IDs. Run simplefin-pp-cli reconcile to detect content-duplicate charges.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you want programmatic, offline, cross-institution access to your own financial data: balances, transactions, holdings, net worth, cash flow, and subscription detection. It is ideal for cron jobs, agent workflows, and plaintextaccounting pipelines where you want a local SQLite database you control rather than a hosted budgeting app.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to move money, pay bills, or transfer funds — SimpleFIN is strictly read-only.
Do not use it to connect a bank for the first time in a browser — that is the SimpleFIN Bridge's /create web flow; this CLI consumes the resulting token.
Do not use it as a budgeting app UI — for full budgeting use Actual Budget or Lunch Money, which can consume SimpleFIN too.
